newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end weaker, unmoved by Iraq row.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end weaker, unmoved by Iraq row.

text.p: Yen-denominated gold futures ended weaker across the board on Wednesday, unfazed by the United States' second missile strike against Iraq, traders said.
Yen-based gold futures ranged from two to five yen per gram lower. Benchmark August was four yen lower at 1,345 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $386.30/60 per ounce at 0718 GMT, against $386.15/386.55 in New York on Tuesday.
"The Iraqi-U.S. row has been confinued locally with little signs of its spreading to other areas; local investors are unlikely to buy gold," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
The gold market has suffered from prolonged static prices, which have thinned volume and open interest of gold futures.
"Private investors are tending to close their positions, pressured by recent static prices," the analyst said.
Platinum and silver futures also ended mostly lower on the heels of gold, amid a lack of fresh incentives.
One trader said some technical buying in platinum after selling gold was detected during the day.
Platinum prices ranged from unchanged to three yen per gram lower. Benchmark August was down two at 1,379 yen.
Silver futures ranged from 0.5 yen to 1.0 yen per 10 grams lower. Benchmark August was 0.5 yen weaker at 184.0 yen.
Traders said views that the upside in spot silver prices was limited also discouraged buying interest in precious metal futures.
They said buying interest in precious metals would remain thin until the market saw a clear direction.
Palladium futures were mixed in directionless trade. Prices ranged from one yen lower to three yen firmer. Benchmark August was one yen firmer at 440 yen.
